review_candidates.title: Senior Civil Service Resilience Associate
review_candidates.description: The Environmental Protection Network (EPN) is composed of more than 800 EPA alumni from across the country who volunteer their time to protect the integrity of EPA and its mission. We harness the expertise of former EPA career staff and confirmation-level appointees from Democratic and Republican administrations to provide the unique perspective of former regulators with decades of historical knowledge and subject matter expertise. EPN is currently focused on building, defending and reimagining the capacity of environmental health agencies and the communities they serve to truly address the most urgent health and environmental crises. We work to ensure that EPA advances policies, programs, budgets, and institutional changes to address climate and environmental injustices, as well as other pressing public health needs. We provide pro bono capacity-building technical assistance and training to frontline communities, NGOs, and under-resourced state/local/tribal government agencies. We offer pro bono support to civil servants. We educate Congress and serve as a critical resource for facts, objective analysis, and scientific rigor for reporters and NGOs. Priority Deadline: December 4th About The Position Reporting to the Civil Service Resilience Manager, the Senior Civil Service Resilience Associate will partner with and act as a support across the civil service resilience efforts. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who loves working in deep collaboration with others and can quickly adapt to changing landscapes and conditions. This staff member will support two main workstreams: First, this person will work closely with our CSR manager to prepare and execute programming for our civil servants, including our job placement & matchmaking, networking & mentorship, career development support, and creating and supporting a community of former EPA civil servants. Second, they will support operational needs across our civil service resilience efforts (including but not limited to scheduling, material creation, outreach, and data entry). Third, they will lead volunteer coordination functions, including in-person gatherings and other regional events for all ten EPA regions as well as HQ and work with an internal team on volunteer recruitment and engagement. Responsibilities General Civil Service Resilience Team Support- Schedule meetings with and draft emails to EPN volunteers and partners. Track projects and accomplishments in EPN’s database and update the database, as needed. Assist with Weekly EPN Updates and Bimonthly Newsletter, as needed. Help with organizing event logistics and operational needs. Community Support & Collective Care- Assist with growing mindfulness and related wellness programming for existing and recent EPA career staff (i.e. Mindlab), as well as staffing weekly Mindlab sessions. Plan and manage the creation and implementation of EPN-sponsored gatherings (including day-maker events) for all ten EPA regions as well as HQ and others tbd. Curating and maintaining updated resources for federal workers. Workforce Development & Career Pathways- Assist in coordinating individualized mentor and coaching support, including follow-up and next steps. Assist with outreach, scoping, scheduling, and moderation of environmental roundtables for colleges and universities with an emphasis on HBCU/MSIs and other regional priority universities. Curating and maintaining effective job placement information and sharing information between partners; updating EPN’s job board weekly (approximately 30 new positions added per week); providing PA team with updated LinkedIn post job board advertisements. Assist Civil Service Resilience Manager with developing and implementing resource webinars and trainings (i.e. scheduling, running slides, monitoring chat/Q&A). Support CSR initiative reimagine workgroup(s) and issue teams. Communications, Organizing & Coalition Building- Attend assigned CSR coalition meetings and report out next steps to appropriate staff Supporting collaboration between partners (i.e. EPA Alumni Association, DOE Alumni Association, FedsForward, UCS, Partnership for Public Service, etc.) Partner with community outreach associates to support our volunteers and civil servants in quickly organizing around critical issues (state and local events, rallies, etc.) Assist in the development of essential resources and frameworks to support our partners, alumni, and volunteers in their efforts to organize peacefully. Volunteer Coordinator- Manage a cross-team committee supporting organizational volunteer engagement Support new volunteer engagement and onboarding (3-4 onboarding meetings per month) Manage all volunteer outreach and communications related to onboarding. Source and recruit volunteers aligned to largest volunteer needs for CSRI and across all EPN programs with a focus on identification and recruitment of the recently separated EPA career staff (4k in the last two years) Support the team with maintaining and updating our internal CRM related to our volunteer engagement efforts. Qualifications At least 2-4 years of relevant work experience Highly productive in remote working environments Self-starter Interest in environmental justice, US environmental and health policy, and/or the work of EPA Experience with or knowledge of social justice and equity issues Strong writing skills Strong project management experience Detail-oriented and unafraid to ask questions Ability to work independently, work on many different projects, and switch effectively from one task to another Experience working in collaborations or with multiple partners Strong work ethic Familiarity with Google Docs and Spreadsheets Prior experience doing volunteer engagement or management (preferred) Core Competencies Building Relationships: The Senior Civil Service Resilience Associate builds and maintains strong relationships with current and former EPA civil servants, volunteers, staff, and external partners. They foster trust, facilitate collaboration, and leverage these connections to strengthen community support, expand access to resources, and advance EPN’s civil service resilience efforts. Making Decisions & Demonstrating Judgment: The Senior Civil Service Resilience Associate demonstrates sound judgment by prioritizing responsibilities, assessing needs, and identifying opportunities to provide meaningful support. They use program data, stakeholder feedback, and an understanding of available resources to connect civil servants and volunteers with appropriate career development, mentorship, wellness, and community support opportunities. Managing Execution: The Senior Civil Service Resilience Associate coordinates and supports the execution of civil service resilience initiatives, including volunteer engagement, regional gatherings, career development programming, and community support activities. They manage operational needs, track progress, coordinate meetings and events, maintain databases, and ensure timely follow-up and collaboration across teams and partners. Planning: The Senior Civil Service Resilience Associate develops and manages plans to balance day-to-day responsibilities and advance key program priorities. They coordinate multiple projects, establish timelines and deliverables, engage stakeholders, monitor progress, and adapt plans as needed to ensure initiatives remain organized, responsive, and aligned with EPN’s goals. Pay An annual salary of $76,934 based in D.C. We will adjust the salary up or down based on locality. Note that this salary is also eligible for a cost-of-living adjustment that would go into effect in 2026. Benefits The Environmental Protection Network is a fully remote virtual environment. We think about our compensation as a package of total rewards that starts with a competitive salary. Work-Life Balance Employees are encouraged to balance a 40-hour work week with a flexible work schedule and core hours of 11 AM-4 PM ET. 11 paid Federal Holidays and other paid days when the office is closed, including: The work day before or after July 4. The day before and after Thanksgiving. The week of December 25th and the week of Jan 1st ( FY27- December 20th-December 31st). Organization-wide non-meeting days on all major holidays that fall outside of the federal calendar (our staff can submit these to our calendar based on religious or cultural holidays). 3 weeks (120 hours) of paid time off (inclusive of sick, personal days, and vacation). 5 days of annual disaster relief time off in the event of a natural disaster impacting you or your family (does not carry over or pay out upon exit). 5 days of annual bereavement (does not carry over or pay out upon exit). 3 annual “EPN” days to be used for any purpose across the year (does not carry over or pay out upon exit). Wellness Benefits 90% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance, 60% employer-paid family. 100% employer-paid life (50K), opportunity to purchase additional life coverage is available for employee and spouse. 100% employer-paid short and long-term disability insurance. Access to employee-paid FSA, HSA, and commuter benefits. Up to 12 weeks of paid leave upon the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child. Career Development Up to $500/year for professional development-related expenses. Ongoing access to internal professional development training. Up to $2,000/year for the purchase of phones, computers, headsets, software, or other equipment used consistently to carry out staff responsibilities and/or wellness-related expenses. Applicable travel expenses will be reimbursed, including travel time outside of your local area. review_candidates.title: Sales Representative & Business Development Manager
review_candidates.description: Company Description Europeum – EDIC is the European consortium responsible for operating and governing the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI), a shared European layer for secure and interoperable digital trust services. EBSI enables public institutions and businesses to exchange and verify trusted data across borders in a transparent and reliable way. Established by the European Commission on 21 May 2024, Europeum brings together 10 EU Member States: Belgium, Cyprus, Greece, Italy, Luxembourg, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, and Spain. The consortium works at the intersection of technology, public policy, and cross-border collaboration to advance trusted digital solutions across Europe. Team members contribute to a dynamic, international environment focused on innovation and public value. Role Description The Sales Representative & Business Development Manager owns the commercial development of EBSI services across the European Union with a sale quota. The role is accountable for building a qualified pipeline of Application Service Providers (ASPs), resellers, public administrations and private-sector adopters, and for converting that  pipeline into signed, recurring commercial agreements. Reporting to the CEO of EUROPEUM-EDIC or his delegate in charge of the sale department, the postholder combines hands-on selling — prospecting, qualifying, negotiating and closing — with the structuring of Europeum's go-to-market: the EBSI Reseller and Partner Programme, offer packaging and pricing, and the commercial side of moving EBSI services from pilot to full production. This is a builder's role in a scale-up European organisation: the successful candidate will be putting the commercial engine in place, not inheriting one. He can leverage the Stakeholder Management and Marketing team to support his sale plan.  Qualifications Demonstrated experience in sales, account management, or business development, preferably in technology, digital services, or public sector solutions. Ability to build and maintain long-term client relationships, manage complex stakeholder environments, and work effectively with cross-functional teams. Strong communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain technical or policy-related concepts in clear business terms. Good understanding of digital transformation, blockchain, or trusted data services; familiarity with EU institutions or public administration is an asset. High level of professional integrity, proactive working style, and ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, international environment. Fluency in English; proficiency in French and/or another EU language is highly beneficial. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Economics, International Relations, Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Willingness to work on-site in Paris and travel within the EU for meetings, events, and business development activities as needed. Key responsibilities 1. Business Development & Pipeline Generation Identify and prioritize commercial opportunities for EBSI use cases across public administrations, EU institutions, system integrators, and private enterprise across the EU-27. Maintain a structured sales pipeline with precise qualification criteria, weighted forecasts, and conversion goals, keeping the CRM strictly updated as the single source of truth. Map decision-maker hierarchies and procurement workflows within target accounts to build actionable account plans. Represent EUROPEUM-EDIC at industry trade shows, European events, and Member State working groups to generate qualified leads. 2. Sales Execution & Closing Manage the complete sales lifecycle from lead qualification to contract execution, including discovery, technical scoping, proposal generation, and negotiation. Lead responses to RFPs, tenders, and commercial quotations in close collaboration with Legal, Finance, and Product teams. Negotiate pricing, SLAs, and commercial terms in alignment with approved guidelines, EUROPEUM-EDIC statutes, and EU procurement rules. Meet or exceed quarterly and annual targets for revenue, signed agreements, and service adoption. 3. Partner, Reseller & Early Adopter Programs Expand the EBSI Partner and Reseller ecosystem by onboarding, training, and managing channel partners and Application Service Providers (ASPs). Transition Early Adopter Program participants from pilot phases into active, paying customers alongside the Stakeholder Management team. Establish joint go-to-market strategies, partner incentive frameworks, and co-selling motions with system integrators. 4. Packaging, Pricing & Market Intelligence Feed direct market feedback into Product Management to refine EBSI service offerings, tiering, and pricing structures. Track regulatory shifts and market trends—including eIDAS 2, EU Digital Identity Wallets, Digital Product Passports, and digital credentials—to unlock new revenue streams. Deliver account-level and industry market research to guide strategic commercial decision-making. 5. Reporting & Commercial Governance Present accurate pipeline metrics, closed deals, and revenue forecasts regularly to the CEO and EUROPEUM-EDIC Assembly. Support the development of annual revenue budgets, commercial strategies, and performance KPIs. Coordinate smooth handoffs to Customer Success and Delivery teams to secure renewals and account expansion. Your Profile Education:  Master's degree in Business Administration, Sales & Marketing, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Experience:  Minimum of 3 to 5 years of experience in B2B and/or B2G sales or business development, with a demonstrable track record of carrying and achieving a quota on complex, long-cycle deals. Public Sector:  Proven experience selling technology services or digital infrastructure to the European public sector, including practical familiarity with EU and national public-procurement rules and tender processes. Channel Management:  Experience building or managing partner, reseller or channel programmes, ideally in a multi-country European setting. Domain Knowledge:  Working understanding of digital trust technologies and regulatory framework (qualified) trust services, blockchain/DLT, verifiable credentials, digital identity, eIDAS with direct EBSI or EUDI Wallet exposure a strong asset. Commercial Rigour:  Consultative selling, pipeline and forecast discipline, business-case and ROI construction, and mastery of a CRM and sales-enablement stack (e.g. HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, LinkedIn Sales Navigator). Environment:  Comfortable operating with high autonomy in a scale-up-like, public-private, multi-cultural environment where processes are still being written. Soft Skills:  Outstanding negotiation, presentation and networking skills; resilience, self-drive, and cultural agility across EU Member States. Languages:  Fluency in English (C1/C2) is essential; French, German or another EU language is a strong plus. What We Offer • The opportunity to work at the core of European digital transformation with a direct impact on the public  services of tomorrow and partnerships with the private sector. • A Fully Flexible Remote position, requiring a location that allows quick access to the headquarters (less than  5 hours travel time to Brussels). • Recurrent travel to Brussels for coordination meetings and European events. • An international, stimulating, and high-growth working environment. • Competitive salary aligned with market standards, complemented by a performance-based variable  component tied to signed business Selection Process Initial Screening:  Review of written applications and CVs to create a shortlist. Interview:  Assessment of leadership capabilities and role fit by the selection committee. Final Selection:  Comprehensive evaluation leading to a target hire by mid-December 2026 and a start date of January 1, 2027. Learn more about the job: https://europeum.eu/

review_candidates.description: Introduction The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunity for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfilment of the wish to return home. The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956 and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with about 6,000 staff. Based in Copenhagen (Denmark) and present in 30 countries, the Danish Refugee Council is a non-profitmaking, politically independent, non-governmental and non-denominational relief organization. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced. All our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation, honesty and transparency. Background Present in Cameroon since 2017, DRC operates in the three complex humanitarian crisis: the conflict in the Lake Chad Basin , the crisis in the North-West and South-West regions (NWSW) , and the impact of the presence of hundreds of thousands of Central African Republic (CAR) refugees in the Eastern façade regions . In Cameroon, DRC ’s interventions are focused on Emergency Response and Durable Solutions via our expertise in protection, economic recovery and peacebuilding. In the Northwest region of Cameroon, DRC is leading the FLASH project which is a localized rapid response mechanism (RRM) for multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) and protection in hard-to-reach areas, implemented through two national partners: SHUMAS and COMINSUD. It combines community early warning system, rapid assessments, emergency cash transfers and protection assistance and response coordination, while strengthening local leadership and response capacity. Looking ahead, FLASH will focus on strengthening risk preparedness, extending displacement analysis to the South-West, and developing a joint strategy with local partners to ensure the mechanism’s sustainability beyond DRC’s potential exit. DRC is envisioning to develop a Nexus approach to contribute to reboot the economic recovery and livelihood of displaced and host populations. Purpose Under the direct supervision of the Country Director, the NWSW Project Manager is responsible for the quality implementation of the "Localised RRM" project in the NWSW regions of Cameroon, as well as for the overall monitoring and capacity strengthening of the two (2) National NGO partners of the project; He/she is also responsible for any contractual, control and accountability aspects related to the implementation of the project as well as driving the reflection for a post emergency/Nexus strategy with the partners and external stakeholders. Additionnally, the NWSW Project manager is responsible for the base management of the Bamenda office and supervises a small team. Duties and Responsibilities PROGRAMMATIC MANAGEMENT: Planning: Prepares, plans and monitors the timely implementation of activities, in close collaboration with the partners, and in a progressive handover perspective. Beneficiary Engagement and Accountability: Oversees that accountability, feedback and reporting mechanisms are put in place and that beneficiaries are engaged with all aspects of the project. Internal coordination: Ensures good coordination and communication within the NW office and the Country Office of DRC Cameroon. External coordination: Ensures excellent coordination and communication with all other humanitarian stakeholders and fora operating in the context of the NWSW region, as well as with local authorities, with emphasis on the effective collaboration and coordination of RRM activities. The programme has two main areas of work: an established dialogue track on military applications of AI and a growing track on civilian advanced AI (‘frontier AI’), convening governments, AI labs and technical experts. Both tracks aim to support and facilitate the adoption of pragmatic and effective national and international measures to address high-priority risks posed by AI for international security, stability and conflict dynamics. As Project Associate you will support the operations and activities of the AIET programme, covering both tracks. You will work within HD’s Technology and International Security, which comprises four programmes: cyber diplomacy; social media and conflict mediation; AI and emerging technologies; and outer space. Key responsibilities are: Support the planning, preparation and delivery of AIET’s consultations, meetings and dialogues with officials, private sector representatives and experts across regions. Support project scoping and development, including mapping issues, stakeholders and key relationships against AIET programme objectives, and drafting concept notes. Monitor key developments relevant to AIET’s work, conduct targeted background research and attend relevant external events. Support the development of AIET’s relationships with government officials, defence / military experts, private sector representatives, multilateral processes, partner organisations, and donors. Support AIET team coordination and work-planning (e.g. keeping abreast of programme work, note-taking during regular meetings, managing documentation, etc.) Support on donor engagement (e.g. drafting project proposals, briefings, and reports). Support on monitoring and evaluation, capturing lessons learnt from across the programme, and liaising with HD’s Mediation Support Unit (MESU). You might be the right person for this role if you: Minimum of 2-3 years’ experience in a similar function in peace and conflict, international security, diplomacy, technology policy or a related area. Politically astute with experience working on diplomacy and/or policy on AI and emerging technologies. Commitment to conflict resolution, peacemaking and related humanitarian issues. Strong writing and analytical skills, including the ability to capture complex issues in a concise form. Excellent organisational skills. Relevant university degree, such as in peace and conflict studies, international relations, technology policy or a related field. Excellent English skills (written and oral); other languages an asset. The position will be based either at HD’s Geneva HQ or remote (location in Central European Time, or a nearby time-zone) and will report to the Head of the AIET Programme.
